diagnostic_bottleneck: Distinguishing between Smut (enlarged spore balls) and Green Ear (malformed panicle) based on the 'green' and 'swollen' description, but the specific 'spherical/ovoid' geometry and 'dense cluster' strongly favor Smut over the diffuse chlorosis/malformation of Green Ear.

final_decision.reason: The observed phenotype of 'spherical/ovoid', 'swollen', 'rounded' structures on the panicle, described as 'bulbous, spherical structure' replacing normal grains, aligns perfectly with the core morphology of Smut (enlarged_spore_ball). The absence of black sclerotia rules out Ergot. The specific geometry (spherical units) contradicts the diffuse nature of Green Ear. Leaf-based diseases (Blast, Rust, Leaf Spots) are ruled out by the primary location on the panicle.

plant_part.specifics: Reproductive head (spike) showing individual florets and developing grains.

symptom_class.description: Florets appear swollen, rounded, and distorted. The normal grain shape is replaced by a bulbous, spherical structure.

geometry.arrangement: Dense cluster on a central axis

surface.texture: Smooth to slightly waxy on the green structures; surrounding chaff appears dry and fibrous.
surface.features: No visible powdery mildew, no obvious raised pustules, no visible black sclerotia (ergot).

texture.observation: The abnormal structures appear firm and turgid (green), contrasting with the dry, brown chaff.

color.abnormality_color: Vivid green, distinct from the surrounding dry tissue.

distribution.pattern: Dense and uniform along the visible length of the panicle.

reproductive_structure.details: Grains/florets are transformed into rounded, green, bulbous bodies. They occupy the position of the grain but are significantly enlarged and spherical compared to normal pearl millet grains.

present: Brown, dry chaff surrounding the green structures
Spherical geometry of the abnormal units
absent: Leafy/vegetative transformation of the entire panicle (Green Ear)
uncertain: Internal contents of the green structures (spore mass vs. tissue)
Whether the green structures are rupturing or intact
